body.x: Clipset, a Spanish technology outlet, selected TOFF MOBILITY, WAVUS and PYUNGHWA GROUP as its top three innovative companies at the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech Into Reality," the third edition combined the Daegu International Future Auto & Mobility Expo (DIFA), the Daegu Robot Expo (ROBEX), the ICT Convergence Expo Korea (ITCE) and start-up programs. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

body.x: Clipset covers smartphones, consumer electronics, digital devices and emerging technologies. It reviews products from a user's perspective and explains complex technology in plain terms.

Juan Castromil, Clipset's editor-in-chief, covered FIX 2026 and also attended FIX 2024. "I witnessed the technology of the future in advance at today's event," he said, praising advances in mobility and control technology.

The three companies Clipset chose cover electric aircraft operation and maintenance, spatial information AI with an urban air mobility (UAM) integrated platform, and functional materials and parts built on automotive parts technology.

body.x: TOFF MOBILITY Offers Operation and Maintenance for Electric Aircraft

TOFF MOBILITY Co., Ltd. is a future aviation mobility company that handles the introduction and distribution of eco-friendly electric aircraft, demonstration flights, maintenance and flight data management. In addition to supplying aircraft, it builds the maintenance and operating systems that flights require.

One of its main services is EV Air Care, an operation and maintenance platform for electric aircraft. It manages maintenance history, battery condition and flight data generated during operations to raise operating efficiency and safety. The company is also developing technology to collect, analyze and manage flight data, such as battery efficiency, environmental variables and maintenance cycles, through an integrated future aviation platform service.

Electric aircraft have the potential to cut noise and carbon emissions in flight compared with internal combustion aircraft. Operating them also requires certification, maintenance systems, charging infrastructure and flight data management. TOFF MOBILITY aims to demonstrate and commercialize electric aviation through a business model that integrates these elements.
The company plans to start with sightseeing, experience and training flights and, over the long term, expand into air travel between regions and islands.

body.x: WAVUS Supports UAM Management With Spatial Information AI and 3D Digital Twins

WAVUS develops platforms that combine spatial information, AI and digital twin technology. In addition to visualizing maps and geographic data, it applies AI to spatial information analysis and uses 3D virtual environments for city and traffic management.

GeOnAI, its spatial information AI solution, is a conversational AI agent that creates customized maps from natural language queries and supports spatial information analysis and preliminary permit diagnosis. Users can request the information they need in natural language and check the analysis results instead of operating complex spatial information systems directly. This can lower the barrier to using specialized spatial information in the public sector, urban planning and industrial sites.

GeOnAirX, another core solution, is a UAM integrated platform built on a 3D digital twin. It recreates real terrain and buildings in three dimensions and supports vertiport site analysis, flight path design and track management. Its functions include weather-reflecting simulation, flight corridor design, and warnings and alternative route guidance in emergencies.

UAM needs digital infrastructure that manages routes, takeoff and landing facilities, surrounding terrain and operating conditions as well as the aircraft. WAVUS combines spatial information AI with digital twins for this purpose.

body.x: PYUNGHWA GROUP Applies Automotive Parts Technology to Robots and Future Mobility

PYUNGHWA GROUP is a group of automotive parts companies that makes anti-vibration systems, hose systems, rubber materials and related parts for cars. It supplies products to the automotive and general industrial machinery sectors, and its main strengths are reducing vibration and noise and improving parts' durability and reliability.

Automotive vibration isolation parts reduce the transmission of vibration from the engine, drivetrain and body to the vehicle and its occupants. Hose systems carry fluids such as fuel and coolant reliably, and different rubber materials and structural designs help parts withstand operating conditions such as temperature, pressure and repeated movement. These technologies are key elements behind a car's ride comfort, durability and safety.

body.x: PYUNGHWA GROUP is extending its materials and design capabilities to new fields such as future mobility and robots. It plans to expand into functional materials and parts for contact and shock absorption in humanoid and quadruped robots.

Robots that work in the same space as people or move in irregular environments need mechanical elements that absorb shock and vibration and improve stability in contact, as well as precise control. Materials technology and durable design from the automotive parts industry can be applied to these needs.
Three Selections Across Aviation, Spatial AI and Parts

Clipset's top three cover electric aircraft operation services, spatial information AI with a UAM integrated platform, and functional materials and parts based on automotive parts. TOFF MOBILITY handles operating and data management services for electric aircraft, WAVUS builds digital infrastructure for air traffic, and PYUNGHWA GROUP makes materials and parts for mobility and robots.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including Clipset. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, editor-in-chief of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, a Chinese outlet for IT, enterprise digital transformation and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, founder and publisher of Pokde.net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.The media partners take part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and plan to report to international audiences on innovative Korean companies in future industries.
